_comment: Curated A15 reference data, hand-authored from the 1996 service manual text layer
(§2-155 to §2-166 for the circuits, §5-2 for the fault codes, §5-21 for the bench
procedure) and checked against Figure 7-18 sheets 1 and 2 and Table 6-19.
The fault codes are the part to read carefully, and the rule is the same one A14's
dataset states: the title is not a verdict. A14 and A15 are a matched pair -- every
relay and control line on A15 is driven from A14, and A15's series-pass circuit
closes A14's magnitude loop -- so the 31xx block names both boards freely. What
decides which board to suspect is which circuit the measurement passes through:
HV MUX0  H4 oven temperature            on A15
HV MUX1  HR7 oven temperature           on A15
HV MUX2  dc HV amplifier output         on A15 (divided by R18/R19)
HV MUX3  series-pass current            on A15 (sensed by R27 and R28)
MUX5     high voltage output            on A14 (its divider and peak detector)
MUX6     absolute value output          on A14
MUX7     AMPLITUDE, reference and error on A14
So a code whose title says A15 but which reads MUX5, MUX6 or MUX7 is testing A14,
and a code titled A14/A15 that reads HV MUX0-3 is testing A15. All seven arrive at
the adc on the DAC assembly (A11) through A14's multiplexer U14 and the SDL line,
which means A14's 3100-3103 group failing makes every other 31xx reading suspect.

overview.summary: The precision analog half of the high-voltage pair, and the board a 1100 V or 2.2 A fault usually ends at. A15 carries two heated-substrate hybrids and the two resistor networks that set the accuracy of three ranges: HR7 with its 70 kohm / 7 Mohm network, which is both the 100:1 dc amplifier for the 1100 V dc range and the 100:1 ac attenuator for the 1100 V ac sense path, and H4 with the 57 ohm / 0.57 ohm network Z5, which gives the 2.2 A range its gain of 100 over A7's 22 mA range. Between them sit the series-pass and current-limit circuit that tells A14's magnitude loop how hard to drive the high-voltage supplies, the 35 mA current limit, the HV OUT / HV SENSE protection clamp, and the AC CAL path through the 399.6 kohm Z6. What A15 does not have is any digital control of its own: all thirteen of its relays -- K1 to K12 and K14 -- and every FET control line are driven from A14, and its four diagnostic points are multiplexed on A14. It cannot be made to do anything without A14 working.
overview.connectors: P601 and P602, DIN 41612 type C, 64-pin right angle, into J601 and J602 on the Analog Motherboard.
overview.note: The board carries the 1100 V output node. HV OUT and HV SENSE both come onto it, three high-voltage cable assemblies (W1, 8.125 in; W2 and W3, 7.375 in) run across it, and TP2 is a dedicated high-voltage socket. §5-21 has you remove the rear shield MP3 and run the board on an extender card, so all of that is exposed and live.

HV.rails: INPUT, HVAMP OUT, +/-SP C, HV OUT / HV SENSE, HV MUX1, HV MUX2, HV MUX3
HV.note: One circuit reconfigured by relays, not two. The HR7 assembly is an op amp on a heated substrate bonded to a 70 kohm / 7 Mohm network; wired one way it is a dc amplifier of -100 for the 1100 V dc range, wired the other it is a 100:1 attenuator for the 1100 V ac sense path. Its output drives the faster U2 to make HVAMP OUT. In dc, K5B routes that to the series-pass circuit and K5A, K7 and K14 put C4 across the 7 Mohm resistor to filter noise; in ac, K9, K8B and K6 add the inverter U1 so OSC SENSE HI is in phase with the Oscillator, and VR7 and VR8 protect the hybrid's input. The series-pass circuit then controls +SP C through Q6 for a positive output and -SP C through Q3 for a negative one, typically about +/-6.8 V dc, and Q4 limits the output at 35 mA by pulling CUR LIM (also called RST) low, which raises PS OFF on A14 and shuts the HVDC supplies down. Q8 drives the HR7 heater with Q9 protecting the hybrid if it fails. CR9, CR10 and R33-R35 hold HV OUT and HV SENSE within 0.7 V of each other if they come apart at the load, and K11 ties them together during ac calibration.

CUR.rails: IHV, G+ / G-, G OUT, B CUR, HV MUX0
CUR.note: The 2.2 A amplifier. A7 is set to its 22 mA range and drives IHV into the 57 ohm portion of Z5; the amplifier forces the same voltage across Z5's 0.57 ohm portion, and the 100:1 ratio makes the current through it 100 times A7's. H4, an op amp on a heated substrate with Q18 driving its heater and Q19 protecting it, produces G OUT -- a voltage proportional to the output current -- and Q22 with R72-R76 forms a high-frequency path for loop stability. U3A and U3B split the H4 signal into two half waves; Q15/R50 and Q16/R48 turn those into currents across the 191 ohm R69 and R56, and U4 and U5 reproduce them a thousand times larger across the 0.1 ohm pairs R68/R78 and R57/R77 through the Darlington pairs Q11/Q12 and Q13/Q14. K12 routes the result to B CUR and back to A7 for binding-post switching. In the dc function only half the circuit is active, since the output is one polarity.

S20.note: The only supply A15 makes for itself, and the only one §5-21 measures: +/-44 S arrive at P602 28A/28C and 29A/29C, drop through the 2 kohm half-watt R31 and R32, and VR3 and VR4 shunt-regulate them to +/-20 V with C15 and C16 across them. They supply U1. Chapter 2 tabulates no supply for this assembly at all, so §5-21 step 2 is the whole published expectation.

VI.note: Made on A14, not here: the stepped-down T1 secondary rectified by A14's CR5 and filtered by its C3 and C4, arriving at P602 18A/18C and 19A/19C with VI COM at 17A/17C. They are low-voltage, high-current rails that source and sink the 2.2 A output, and their magnitude is deliberately held down by A14's magnitude control loop to keep the collector-emitter voltage low on Q11 and Q14. That is why they are not a fixed rail and why a reading only means anything at a stated output current.

COM.rails: ACOM, PACOM, SCOM, RLH COM, VI COM
COM.note: ACOM is the reference for every §5-21 measurement unless a step says otherwise, and it is not permanently tied to anything: K3 connects it to RCOM in the dc voltage function and K3 with K4A connect it to OSC RCOM in the ac function. CR5 and CR6, back to back, keep ACOM and PACOM within a diode drop of each other.

faultCodes.title: A15: HV Oven Regulation Fault
faultCodes.measure: The HR7 hybrid's heater voltage is divided by 11 -- R15 (100 kohm) over R16 (10 kohm) -- to make HV MUX1, and read by the adc on the DAC assembly through A14's multiplexer.
faultCodes.verdict: Out of tolerance means A15 is probably at fault. This is the HR7 oven, so suspect Q8, Q9 and the +8 RLH feed before the hybrid itself. Check the oven cover is fitted: running the board with it off changes the thermal load and can fail this code on a good hybrid.

faultCodes.title: A15: HV I Oven Regulation Fault
faultCodes.measure: The H4 hybrid's heater voltage goes to A14 as HV MUX0, is switched onto SDL and read by the adc on the DAC assembly. Divided here by R39 (100 kohm) over R40 (10 kohm).
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A15 is probably at fault -- the same circuit as 3104 but for the 2.2 A hybrid: Q18 drives the heater and Q19 protects it. 3104 and 3105 failing together points at the +8 RLH supply they share rather than at either oven.

faultCodes.title: A15: DC HV Amp Noise Fault
faultCodes.measure: Both high-voltage assemblies are put in the dormant state except that the DAC output, set to 0.0 V, is connected to the dc HV amplifier / ac sense buffer configured for a gain of 100, with its output on the RCL line. The adc takes ten readings.
faultCodes.expected: The spread between the lowest and the highest of the ten readings is 0.001 V or less
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A15 is probably at fault. This is a noise test on the HR7 hybrid and U2, not a gain or offset test -- 3106, 3107 and 3108 are three different complaints about the same circuit in the same configuration, and which of them fires tells you which.

faultCodes.title: A15: DC HV Amp Offset Fault
faultCodes.measure: Same configuration as 3106; the average of the ten adc readings is taken.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A15 is probably at fault. Offset at a gain of 100 means 30 uV at the amplifier input, which is what the heated substrate exists to hold -- so an offset failure with 3104 also failing is an oven problem, and an offset failure on its own is the hybrid.

faultCodes.title: A15: DC HV Amp Gain Fault
faultCodes.measure: Same configuration, but the DAC is set to -0.001 V, so a gain of -100 should give 0.1 V on the RCL line. The gain is computed from that reading and the offset measured in 3107.
faultCodes.expected: Computed gain within 6% of the nominal -100
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A15 is probably at fault. Gain here is the ratio of the 7 Mohm and 70 kohm resistors inside the HR7 assembly, so a genuine gain failure is a hybrid replacement -- but check first that K1, K5, K7 and K14 are in the positions the dc configuration wants, because a relay that has not moved looks exactly like a wrong ratio.

faultCodes.title: A15: HV +DC Preamplifier Fault
faultCodes.measure: dc 1100 V range at +220 V, +600 V and +1100 V. The dc HV amplifier output is divided by R18 and R19 into HV MUX2, routed to A14's diagnostic multiplexer and read on SDL.
faultCodes.verdict: A15. This is the same node and the same number as §5-21 step 10's +220 V dc check at TP3, so the bench check and the self test agree by construction -- if the code fires and TP3 reads 0.55 V, suspect the R18/R19 divider or the HV MUX2 path rather than the amplifier.

faultCodes.title: A15: HV +DC Series Pass & Current Fault
faultCodes.measure: dc 1100 V range at +220 V, +600 V and +1100 V. HV MUX3 comes from the HV dc output series pass and current limit circuit, where R28 senses the current for a positive output.
faultCodes.verdict: A15. HV MUX3 monitors the current drawn through the series-pass circuit to catch an overcurrent, so this firing at all three amplitudes suggests the sense chain; firing only at 1100 V suggests something really is drawing current.

faultCodes.title: A15: HV +DC High Voltage Output Fault
faultCodes.measure: dc 1100 V range at +220 V, +600 V and +1100 V. The output is divided into MUX5 -- A14's divider and output peak measure circuit -- and read on SDL.
faultCodes.verdict: Titled A15, but measured entirely through A14. If the output really is present and correct at the binding posts, suspect A14's MUX5 chain rather than anything here. What would convict A15 is this firing together with 3109 or 3110.

faultCodes.title: A15: HV +DC Ref/Error Amplitude Fault
faultCodes.measure: dc 1100 V range at +220 V, +600 V and +1100 V. AMPLITUDE, from A14's magnitude control, is divided into MUX7 and read on SDL. The nominal AMPLITUDE-to-HV OUT gain is 135.
faultCodes.verdict: Titled A15, but this is A14's reference and error amplifier. It can still be A15's fault indirectly: AMPLITUDE is what the loop settles at, and the loop is closed through this board's series-pass circuit, so a stuck +/-SP C moves AMPLITUDE without anything on A14 being wrong. Check TP4 and TP6 before condemning A14.

faultCodes.title: A15: HV -DC Preamplifier Fault
faultCodes.measure: As 3109 but at -220 V, -600 V and -1100 V.
faultCodes.verdict: A15. The same node as §5-21 step 10's -220 V dc check at TP3. The two polarities give different numbers (0.55 V and 2.3 V) because the amplifier is not symmetric about zero here; that is not a fault.

faultCodes.title: A15: HV -DC Series Pass & Current Fault
faultCodes.measure: As 3110 but at -220 V, -600 V and -1100 V. R27 senses the current for a negative output.
faultCodes.verdict: A15. 3110 and 3114 firing together is the sense chain or the multiplexer; one without the other separates R28's half from R27's, and therefore Q6's side from Q3's.

faultCodes.title: A15: HV -DC High Voltage Output Fault
faultCodes.measure: As 3111 but at -220 V, -600 V and -1100 V, through A14's MUX5.
faultCodes.verdict: Titled A15, measured through A14. Firing on one polarity only points at the polarity selection relays K4 and K11 on A14 rather than at anything on this board.

faultCodes.title: A15: HV -DC Reference/Error Amp Fault
faultCodes.measure: As 3112 but at -220 V, -600 V and -1100 V, through A14's MUX7.
faultCodes.verdict: A14's reference and error amplifier again, with the same caveat as 3112: the loop closes through this board. 3112 and 3116 together, both polarities, is a strong pointer at A14's integrator; one polarity only is more likely to be Q3 or Q6 here.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15: HV +DC Current Error Amp Fault
faultCodes.measure: dc +2.2 A range at +0.22 A, +0.6 A and +1.2 A. AMPLITUDE via A14's MUX7.
faultCodes.expected: AMPLITUDE within ±25% of the expected value
faultCodes.verdict: A14's reference and error amplifier in the current function. What makes it A15's business is that AMPLITUDE in this function is set by the VI+ / VI- headroom the loop needs over Q11 and Q14, so a shorted or leaky output device here moves it. Check TP9 and TP10 at a stated output before assuming A14.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15: HV -DC Current Error Amp Fault
faultCodes.measure: dc -2.2 A range at -1.2 A. AMPLITUDE via A14's MUX7.
faultCodes.expected: AMPLITUDE within ±25% of the expected value
faultCodes.verdict: As 3117, negative polarity, which exercises the other half of the output stage: Q13 and Q14 through U5 rather than Q11 and Q12 through U4.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15: HV +DC Current Abs. Value
faultCodes.measure: dc 2.2 A range at 0.22 A, 0.60 A and 1.2 A into the 1.2 ohm load on the Current assembly. G OUT from this board drives A14's absolute value circuit, whose output is divided into MUX6.
faultCodes.verdict: The measurement is A14's absolute value circuit, but the signal is A15's G OUT. Scope TP11 first: if G OUT is proportional to the output current, the fault is A14's; if it is not, it is the H4 hybrid or the output stage here. §5-20 step 4 on A14 is the bench version of exactly this comparison.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15: HV -DC Current Abs. Value
faultCodes.measure: dc -2.2 A range at -1.2 A, otherwise as 3119. The absolute value output is a positive voltage in both cases.
faultCodes.verdict: As 3119. The output being positive for a negative current is the point of the absolute value circuit, not a fault. Only one of U3A and U3B is active for a given dc polarity, so 3119 without 3120 or vice versa separates the two halves of the half-wave splitter.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15: HV AC 1 kHz, Preamp (Lo)
faultCodes.measure: ac 1100 V range at 220 V, 1 kHz. The dc HV amplifier / ac sense buffer output is divided into HV MUX2 and read on SDL.
faultCodes.verdict: A15. HV MUX2 is a dc measurement of an ac node, so 0 V is what a correctly working ac sense buffer gives -- this checks that the buffer is not sitting at a dc offset, not that it is passing signal. §5-21 step 8 is the check that it is passing signal.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15: HV AC 1 kHz, Preamp (Mid)
faultCodes.measure: ac 1100 V range at 600 V, 1 kHz, via HV MUX2.
faultCodes.verdict: A15, as 3122. The three 1 kHz amplitudes test the same circuit at three signal levels; all three failing is the buffer, one failing is more likely the range switching.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15: HV AC 1 kHz, Preamp (Hi)
faultCodes.measure: ac 1100 V range at 1100 V, 1 kHz, via HV MUX2.
faultCodes.verdict: A15, as 3122. Failing only at 1100 V, with the Lo and Mid cases passing, points at the input protection VR7 and VR8 clamping, or at the HV OUT / HV SENSE clamp R33-R35 loading the node.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15: HV AC 100 Hz, Preamp (Lo)
faultCodes.measure: ac 1100 V range at 220 V. The title says 100 Hz; the body of the code says 50 Hz -- see the caveat.
faultCodes.verdict: A15. Below 120 Hz A14's K14-K16 series the transformer windings, so this trio failing while the 1 kHz trio passes points at those three relays on A14 rather than at the buffer here.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15: HV AC 100 Hz, Preamp Fault
faultCodes.measure: ac 1100 V range at 600 V, 50 Hz per the body of the code, via HV MUX2.
faultCodes.verdict: A15. The odd one out by name: the other five in this group are labelled (Lo), (Mid) or (Hi) and this one is not, but it is the 600 V case of the low-frequency trio.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15: HV AC 100 Hz, Preamp (Hi)
faultCodes.measure: ac 1100 V range at 1100 V, 50 Hz per the body of the code, via HV MUX2.
faultCodes.verdict: A15. As 3124 but at low frequency; the same input-protection suspects apply.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15: HV AC 1 kHz, Output (Lo)
faultCodes.measure: ac 1100 V range at 220 V, 1 kHz. The output is divided and peak-detected by A14 into MUX5.
faultCodes.verdict: The manual says outright that a failure indicates A14 is probably at fault. Read this group alongside 3122-3124: the Preamp trio and the Output trio look at the same high voltage through different circuits, so Preamp passing and Output failing is A14's peak detector, and both failing is the high voltage really being wrong.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15: HV AC 1 kHz, Output (Mid)
faultCodes.measure: ac 1100 V range at 600 V, 1 kHz, via A14's MUX5.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A14 is probably at fault.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15: HV AC 1 kHz, Output (Hi)
faultCodes.measure: ac 1100 V range at 1100 V, 1 kHz, via A14's MUX5.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A14 is probably at fault -- its transformer and range relays rather than its peak detector if only the Hi case fires.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15: HV AC 100 Hz, Output (Lo)
faultCodes.measure: ac 1100 V range at 220 V. Titled 100 Hz, specified at 50 Hz in the body. Via A14's MUX5.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A14 is probably at fault: below 120 Hz its K14-K16 series the transformer windings, so this trio failing while the 1 kHz trio passes is a pointer straight at those relays.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15: HV AC 100 Hz, Output (Mid)
faultCodes.measure: ac 1100 V range at 600 V, 50 Hz per the body of the code, via A14's MUX5.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A14 is probably at fault.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15: HV AC 100 Hz, Output (Hi)
faultCodes.measure: ac 1100 V range at 1100 V, 50 Hz per the body of the code, via A14's MUX5.
faultCodes.verdict: A failure indicates A14 is probably at fault.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15/A16: 2.2 A AC Range Mag. Fault
faultCodes.measure: ac 2.2 A range at 0.22 A, 0.6 A and 1.1 A at 1 kHz, 0.6 A at 40 Hz and 1.1 A at 50 Hz, into the 1.2 ohm load. The input current from A7 is measured as the drop across A7's 22 mA range shunt.
faultCodes.verdict: Titled across three assemblies, but the manual says a failure indicates A15 is probably at fault. It is measuring what A7 delivers into this board's input, so what it really tests is whether the 2.2 A amplifier is loading IHV correctly -- Z5's 57 ohm portion and the H4 input.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15/A16: 2.2 A AC Range Compliance
faultCodes.measure: Same five ac settings. The compliance voltage is measured on the output side of A7's 22 mA shunt through the Current Compliance Monitor on A7.
faultCodes.verdict: The manual says a failure indicates A15 is probably at fault. Compliance running away means the output stage cannot deliver into the load: suspect the Darlington pairs Q11/Q12 and Q13/Q14, the 0.1 ohm sense resistors, or the VI rails being too low.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15/A16: 2.2 A AC Range Amplitude
faultCodes.measure: Same five ac settings. G OUT is routed to A14's magnitude control and AMPLITUDE is read via MUX7.
faultCodes.verdict: A14's reference and error amplifier in the 2 A ac function. It is fed from this board's G OUT, so check TP11 before A14 -- but the affine expected value (a slope and an offset) is the signature of A14's loop rather than of anything here.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15/A16: 2.2 A AC Range Abs. Value
faultCodes.measure: Same five ac settings. G OUT drives A14's absolute value circuit, whose output is divided into MUX6.
faultCodes.verdict: A14's absolute value circuit, driven by A15's G OUT. The tightest tolerance in the whole 2.2 A group at ±10%, so it is often the first of the pair to fire and is worth reading as an early warning rather than as a verdict.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15/A16: 2.2 A DC Range Dummy Load
faultCodes.measure: dc 2.2 A range into the 1.2 ohm load on the Current assembly. The voltage across the load is brought to SDL as DUMMY LOAD and read by the adc, and the current computed from it.
faultCodes.verdict: The manual says a failure indicates A15 is probably at fault. This is the most direct measurement of what the 2.2 A amplifier is actually delivering, so a failure here with 3143 passing is unusual and worth distrusting.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15/A16: 2.2 A DC Range Compliance
faultCodes.measure: dc 2.2 A range into the 1.2 ohm load. Compliance measured on the output side of A7's 22 mA shunt through the Current Compliance Monitor.
faultCodes.verdict: The manual says a failure indicates A15 is probably at fault. The dc counterpart of 3138; in dc only one half of the output stage conducts, so 3142 failing while 3138 passes narrows it to one polarity's Darlington.

faultCodes.title: A14/A15/A16: 2.2 A DC Range Magnitude
faultCodes.measure: dc 2.2 A range. The output current is computed from the drop across A7's 22 mA range shunt.
faultCodes.verdict: The manual says a failure indicates A15 is probably at fault. With 3141 it forms a pair that measures the same current two ways -- at the load and at the input shunt -- so both failing is the amplifier and one failing is the measurement path.

componentNotes.HR7: The high-voltage dc hybrid: an op amp on a heated substrate bonded to a 70 kohm / 7 Mohm resistor network. It sets the accuracy of both the 1100 V dc and the 1100 V ac range, and it is the part §5-21 spends five of its fourteen steps around. Table 6-19 marks it ESD-sensitive; it is a single stock number (775254) and not field-repairable.
componentNotes.H4: The 2.2 A hybrid: an LT1007-class op amp on a heated substrate, stock 813444. Note that the parts list files it under the H designator family, which on this board is otherwise screws and rivets, so the type legend shows it as mechanical -- see the caveat.
componentNotes.Z5: R-net / heat sink assembly 4R03: the 57 ohm and 0.57 ohm sections that set the 2.2 A range's 100:1 ratio, and therefore its accuracy. §5-21 step 12 has you lift R37 at the node it shares with Z5 pins 2 and 3.
componentNotes.Z6: R-net / heat sink assembly 4R23. Two things at once: the 399.6 kohm AC CAL resistor that feeds A12's 400 ohm rms sensor during ac calibration, and the heat sink Q11 is mounted to. See the caveat about its stock number.
componentNotes.C4: 0.022 uF at 1500 V, across the 7 Mohm feedback resistor in the HR7 assembly when K5A, K7 and K14 put it there for the dc function. A polypropylene part with a real voltage rating -- do not substitute a 50 V polyester.
componentNotes.C34: 22 uF 10 V tantalum on +5 RLH. Worth attention in a recap: +5 RLH runs at about 6 V, which is 60% of the part's rating -- the same exposure as A14's C13.
componentNotes.C30: 10 uF 35 V tantalum on +15 S, running at about 43% of rating. Comfortable.
componentNotes.C31: 10 uF 35 V tantalum on -15 S. See C30.
componentNotes.C37: 10 uF 35 V tantalum on VI+, which is nominally about 5 V. Very lightly stressed and low priority in a recap.
componentNotes.C39: 10 uF 35 V tantalum on VI-. See C37.
componentNotes.Q4: The 35 mA current limit. When it trips it pulls CUR LIM (also called RST) low, which raises PS OFF on A14 and shuts down HVCL and with it the HVDC supplies. An instrument that keeps collapsing its high-voltage output may be limiting correctly rather than failing -- check Q4 before suspecting the amplifier chain.
componentNotes.Q8: TIP32A driving the HR7 oven heater.
componentNotes.Q9: TIP120 that protects the HR7 hybrid if Q8 fails.
componentNotes.Q18: TIP32A driving the H4 oven heater.
componentNotes.Q19: TIP120 that protects the H4 hybrid if Q18 fails.
componentNotes.Q11: One of the two 2.2 A output devices, mounted to the Z6 heat sink assembly. Table 6-19 note 1 makes it part of assembly 665489 along with the thermal insulator MP10, the clamp bar MP22 and the screws H1/H2 -- do not remount it without the correct insulator.
componentNotes.Q14: The other 2.2 A output device. The schematic annotates it 'MOUNTED TO Z7', a designator that does not exist in the parts list -- see the caveat.
componentNotes.R37: 825 ohm metal film at the H4 input, on the G+ node with Z5 pins 2 and 3. This is the resistor §5-21 step 12 has you unsolder at one end to inject an external reference. Resolder it and refit the H4 cover before continuing.
componentNotes.R2: 100 kohm in series with the high-voltage test point TP2. It is a safety and loading resistor, and it is why TP2 is not a place to make the ±0.1 V measurement of §5-21 step 8.
componentNotes.MP3: The rear high-voltage shield. It has to come off to troubleshoot, and the board is then live and exposed on the extender card.
componentNotes.MP10: Thermal insulator under the high-voltage output devices, part of the Z6 assembly 665489.
componentNotes.MP22: High-voltage clamp bar, part of the Z6 assembly 665489.
componentNotes.W1: High-voltage cable assembly, 8.125 in. One of three that run across the board carrying the 1100 V nodes.

caveats.title: §5-21 and §2-161 disagree about which half of U3 shows which peaks
caveats.text: §5-21 step 13 says pin 7 of U3B displays a square wave equal to the positive peaks of Figure 5-32 and pin 1 of U3A the negative peaks. §2-161 says the opposite: U3A creates the half wave equal to the positive peaks of the H4 signal, held about 0.7 V above 0 V by R47, and U3B subtracts it to leave the half wave equal to the negative peaks, held about 0.7 V below 0 V by R45. The two can be reconciled if the theory is describing which peaks each half wave is derived from while the procedure is describing which way up the trace appears on the scope, since U3A's stage inverts -- but the manual never says so, and nothing here picks a winner. Both statements are recorded on the two probe points. What the step is really checking is that a half wave appears at each pin at all.

caveats.title: The schematic mounts Q14 on a Z7 that does not exist
caveats.text: Sheet 2 annotates Q11 'MOUNTED TO Z6' and Q14 'MOUNTED TO Z7'. Table 6-19 lists only Z5 and Z6, and its note 1 says assembly 665489 -- which is Z6 -- contains part numbers 761296, 797829, 454041, 454033, 760850 and 320051. Those are the R-net itself, the thermal insulator MP10, Q11 (454041), Q14 (454033), the clamp bar MP22 and the screws H1/H2. So both output transistors are part of the Z6 assembly, and Z7 on the schematic is either a second heat sink that was never given a parts-list line or a leftover from an earlier revision. Order 665489 and you get the whole thing either way.

caveats.title: Z6 is one stock number in the 1996 list and a different one in Rev 9
caveats.text: Table 6-19 (1996) gives Z6 as 665489, R-NET/HEAT SINK ASSY-4R23, with the note that 665489 is an assembly containing 761296 and five other parts. The Rev 9 list gives Z6 as 761296 -- the bare R-net -- with the same description. They are not the same purchase: 761296 is the resistor network alone and 665489 is the network plus the insulator, both output transistors, the clamp bar and its screws. The dataset records 761296 as the Rev 9 'as built' number, but if you are replacing a damaged heat sink assembly, 665489 is the number that gets you a complete one.

caveats.title: Twenty-eight parts have different Fluke stock numbers in the two revisions
caveats.text: Almost every carbon-film and metal-film resistor on this board changed stock number between the 1996 list and Rev 9 -- R1/R72 (343426 in 1996, 573170 in Rev 9), R2/R15/R39 (348920 / 573584), R4 and its group (348771 / 573014), and so on through R73/R75 -- along with the 1N4448 diode groups (203323 / 698720), the H1/H2 screws (320051 / 152173), VR3/VR4 (180463 / 832576), VR7/VR8 (325837 / 698712) and Z6. The descriptions are identical in every case except Z6 and the screws, which reads as a supplier renumbering rather than a design change. Rev 9 is the revision the drawing and the photograph match, so its numbers are recorded as 'as built'.

caveats.title: Q11's power rating differs between the two parts lists and neither is flagged
caveats.text: The 1996 Table 6-19 gives Q11 as TRANSISTOR,SI,BV=100V,50W,TO-220; the Rev 9 list prints BV=100V, 2W,TO-220 for the same stock number 454041 and the same manufacturer part, MJE15029. Because the stock numbers agree, the two rows join cleanly and the difference never reaches the dataset as an 'as built' entry -- it is only visible by reading both pages. An MJE15029 is a 50 W device, so the Rev 9 line is a typo; it is recorded here because a 2 W rating would make the part look wrongly specified for a 2.2 A output stage.

caveats.title: The note after step 8 renumbers the steps it is pointing at
caveats.text: The Note between steps 8 and 9 says 'Steps 10 through 12 check the High Voltage/High Current assembly in the 1100V dc range'. The dc range steps as printed are 9, 10 and 11 -- step 9 checks the input voltage at TP1, step 10 the amplifier at TP3 and step 11 ±SP C -- and step 12 is the first of the 2.2 A checks, which the next Note correctly calls 'Steps 12 through 14'. So the first Note is off by one at both ends. §5-21's own step numbers are used throughout this dataset; the Note is the thing that is wrong.

caveats.title: Steps 7 and 8 name a TP9 and a TP10 that are not this board's
caveats.text: The workaround for the instrument tripping into standby during the 1100 V ac check is 'connecting a jumper from TP9 to TP10 on the DAC assembly'. A15 has its own TP9 and TP10 -- VI+ and VI- -- and the automatic reference extraction cannot tell the difference, so those two designators appear as clickable references on steps 7 and 8 of the procedure and will take you to the wrong board. The step text says 'on the DAC assembly (A11)' and that is the authority. Jumpering A15's TP9 to its TP10 would short VI+ to VI-.

caveats.title: Fault codes 3125 to 3127 and 3131 to 3133 are titled 100 Hz and specify 50 Hz
caveats.text: All six are titled 'HV AC 100Hz', and all six bodies configure the instrument at 50 Hz. Nothing else distinguishes them from 3122-3124 and 3128-3130, which are the same three amplitudes at 1 kHz. Either way the group tests operation below 120 Hz, where A14's K14-K16 series the transformer windings, so what it tells you is the same; but if you are reproducing the condition by hand, the body is the specific instruction and the title is not. The same discrepancy is recorded in A14's dataset.

caveats.title: Fault code 3121 is listed as an A15 code and is not one
caveats.text: The 31xx block runs 3100 to 3143 with two gaps. 3121 and 3134 are both printed as 'Spare -- This fault code is not used'. They are noted here because a table of contents or an index that lists the block as a range will suggest they exist.

caveats.title: H4 is a hybrid that the type legend files under Mechanical
caveats.text: Designator kinds are derived from the prefix, and on every assembly covered so far the H family has been screws, rivets and standoffs -- so H maps to 'mechanical'. A15 is the first board where an H designator is an active device: H4 is the 2.2 A hybrid, an op amp on a heated substrate. Its parts-list description says so and its function note says so, but the marker colour and the type filter both treat it as mechanical. HR7, the other hybrid, does not have this problem: HR is a new prefix on this board and is filed with the resistor networks, which is what the schematic calls it ('HR7 RNET 70K 7M').

caveats.title: How far each set of positions was checked
caveats.text: Board: every one of the 236 parts is accounted for -- 208 markers reviewed by eye and 28 recorded as having no silkscreen designator. The reader placed 148 and 125 of those survived review; 109 were placed or corrected by hand, including all eleven test points. Schematic sheet 1: all 103 machine placements reviewed one by one, 83 kept, and five parts placed by hand (TP1, TP5, U1, U2, Q9). Sheet 2: all 120 reviewed, 86 kept, two placed by hand (TP9, TP10). The four hand-placed test points were each checked against the zone the sheet 1 legend prints for them and all four agree. No second reader was run on this board -- the vision-language cross-check was not needed for the board, which read well enough to review directly, and was not attempted on the sheets. Every marker carries the tier it came from and the app shows it.

caveats.title: Manufacturer part numbers come from OCR of a scan and carry character errors
caveats.text: The 1996 parts list has a real text layer, so its designators, descriptions and Fluke stock numbers are exact. The manufacturer supply code and manufacturer part number exist only in the scanned Rev 9 list, and at that type size the reader confuses 0 with O and 5 with S and picks up column rules as stray letters. Four rows lost their manufacturer columns entirely: R23, R24, R60 and R65 share a Rev 9 row whose stock number is scanned with an extra leading digit ('1572941' for 572941), so the row never parsed. Five more -- MP11, MP12 and the three cable ties MP14-MP16 -- have no Rev 9 line at all. The Fluke stock number is the identifier to order against.

caveats.title: The photograph is aligned from eight landmarks and is approximate
caveats.text: Nothing covers this board in the photograph -- the rear shield is off -- but the two moulded hybrid covers and the two heat sink assemblies are fitted, so HR7, H4, Z5, Z6, Q11, Q14 and everything under the covers is hidden even though the markers sit in the right places. The alignment is a homography fitted from eight label centres judged by eye (the ends of the test point row, TP11, the K9/K6/K11 cluster, P602 and K10), and the photograph is not a perfectly overhead shot, so expect a marker to land on the right part rather than on the middle of it.
